query_text: What quantitative models or empirical correlations have been developed to predict PP blend properties from component characteristics?
draft:
Several quantitative models and empirical correlations have been developed to predict the properties of polypropylene (PP) blends, though the retrieved literature primarily focuses on binary PP/polyethylene (PE) systems, virgin/recycled PP blends, and PP composites rather than specific ternary blends of virgin homopolymer, impact copolymer, and post-consumer recycled PP (PCR-PP).

For basic mechanical properties, the Law of Mixtures has been shown to accurately predict the elastic modulus of virgin and recycled PP blends in the elastic deformation region [Paper12]. To predict Young's modulus across various blend morphologies, researchers have utilized Veenstra's model, Davies' equation, and Kolarik's geometrical models (the Cross Orthogonal Skeleton and Three Perpendicular Plates models), which rely on component volume fractions and morphological descriptors [Paper50]. For impact strength, a preliminary model predicts blend toughness based on the impact strengths of the pure components, their volume fractions, and the continuity degree of the PP phase [Paper50]. 

More complex mechanical behaviors are addressed by extending existing theoretical frameworks. Richeton's statistical stiffness model, combined with the Tandon-Weng approach, predicts the elastic behavior of PP-based composites by accounting for temperature, strain-rate, filler content, and reprocessing cycles [Paper227]. Similarly, Gueguen's cooperative model, integrated with the Pukanszhy approach, estimates compressive yield stress under varying strain rates and recycling conditions [Paper227]. 

For physical and thermal properties, an empirical equation by Wong and Lam estimates the overall crystallinity of PP/PE systems, while an additive rule accurately describes blend density [Paper89]. Additive models have also been applied to predict the rheological and mechanical properties of virgin PP blended with reprocessed PP [Paper147]. 

Data-driven and statistical approaches are also utilized to model blend properties. Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models have been developed to predict the mechanical and physical properties of recycled polymer blends with high accuracy [Paper3]. Multiple regression models have been used to quantify how residual PE in recycled PP affects elongation at break [Paper122], and mathematical models based on rheometric measurements (cross-over point and zero-shear viscosity) can determine polyethylene contamination levels in PP [Paper207]. Additionally, Taguchi-Grey Relational Analysis has been employed to optimize blend compositions involving crosslinking agents and compatibilizers [Paper3].

The provided excerpts do not contain quantitative models specifically tailored to ternary blends of virgin impact copolymer PP, virgin homopolymer PP, and PCR-PP. To fully answer the query for the target application, additional data detailing the specific phase interactions, empirical mixing rules, and morphological development of these three specific components would be required.
